headline: Light showers Tuesday, then warm, dry days Thursday and Friday before wetter weekend weather.
summary: A weather system passing through British Columbia clips the region with light showers Tuesday into early Wednesday, mostly along the coast, the west side of the Olympics, and northward from King County. Amounts stay small. High pressure then rebuilds, and showers fade Wednesday. Thursday and Friday look warm, with highs mostly in the mid 60s to mid 70s, as air flows off the land toward the coast. Friday runs about 5 to 10 degrees above normal, and the warm spell looks likely. The weekend turns wetter: a weak system may bring rain Saturday, mainly to the coast and North Cascades, and a stronger one Sunday into Monday brings more widespread rain and breezy winds, with highs only in the upper 50s to mid 60s. Mountain snow is possible, and the weekend is less certain.
